source: TRAI national numbering plan summaries and public telecom documentation
notes: Categories describe how a series is allocated, not whether a call is fraudulent. Heuristic entries are user observations and are shipped disabled.

rules.name: 1600 Transactional Service
rules.description: Transactional and service calls from banking, financial services, insurance and government. Not promotional traffic.

rules.name: 1601 Transactional Service
rules.description: Transactional and service calls from sectors other than BFSI and government.

rules.name: 1800 Toll Free
rules.description: Indian toll-free service numbers. Usually a company's own customer service line.

rules.name: 140 Promotional Calls
rules.description: The regulated Indian series for promotional and telemarketing calls. Blocking it stops marketing, not service messages.

rules.name: 0900 Premium Rate
rules.description: Premium-rate service series. Calls in this range can be chargeable.

rules.name: Unknown callers
rules.description: Calls where the network supplied no usable caller ID. Off by default because it also catches some legitimate callers.

rules.name: Private callers
rules.description: Callers who have deliberately withheld their number.

rules.name: International callers
rules.description: Any caller with a country code other than +91. International is not the same as unwanted, so this is off by default.
